synthesis.consensus: Across the provided literature, a distinct transition in deformation behavior for High-Entropy Alloys occurs in the elevated temperature regime, specifically centered around or above 700 °C. Below this threshold, materials exhibit limited work softening, while above it, mechanisms such as Dynamic Recrystallization (DRX) and the formation of specific dislocation networks (cellular/columnar structures) become prominent.
synthesis.different_approaches: The papers approach the question from different material systems and analytical angles. A second study on the refractory Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti HEA focuses on the cessation of cavitation at 1000–1200 °C, attributing it to DRX but acknowledging the lack of explicit causal proof for excluding other healing mechanisms [0a10fd456fa9c8d0]. A third study on SLM-built CoCrFeMnNi provides specific microstructural observations of dislocation networks and cellular structures emerging above 700 °C, correlating this with the onset of work softening [14ba0832e6e2cfff, 6b139b17e2d2f29f].
synthesis.condition_dependencies: The mechanisms are strictly dependent on temperature thresholds. In CoCrFeMnNi, work softening (potentially linked to DRX) is observed only at temperatures higher than 700 °C, implying conditions were not met at 650 °C [14ba0832e6e2cfff]. In Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti, the disappearance of cavitation and occurrence of DRX are explicitly linked to the 1000–1200 °C range [0a10fd456fa9c8d0].
synthesis.contradictions: No direct contradictions are found in the data, but there is a variation in the precision of mechanistic claims. While the Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti alloy analysis observes DRX concurrent with cavitation disappearance, it explicitly states the causal link is not defined [0a10fd456fa9c8d0], whereas the CoCrFeMnNi analysis infers the softening is 'potentially DRX' based on temperature thresholds [14ba0832e6e2cfff]. synthesis.evidence_strength: The evidence is moderate.
